newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy signs new Philip Morris deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy signs new Philip Morris deal.

text.p: Italy on Thursday renewed a long-running deal with Philip Morris Cos Inc to produce the U.S. tabacco group's cigarettes under licence, despite investigations into allegations the company had defrauded the treasury.

The finance ministry said in a statement that after months of negotiations, the state tabacco department Monopoli had signed a new two-year accord which "significantly cut" the royalties it paid Philip Morris.
It gave no financial details, but Italian newsagency Ansa said that under the terms of the deal, Philip Morris had reduced royalities on some of its products by two percentage points.
In addition, it had agreed to waver some five billion lire ($2.9 million) in interest due on delayed payments, Ansa said.
Philip Morris, which makes the Marlboro brand, controls about 50 percent of the Italian cigarette market with sales of some 10 trillion lire in 1995.

Relations between the U.S. firm and the Italian authorities soured last year when magistrates in Rome, Naples and Milan started looking into claims that Philip Morris avoided paying taxes on around 10 trillion lire of revenues since 1987.
Philip Morris denies any wrong-doing and has blasted Italy's complex, costly tax system. Magistrates are continuing their investigations.

Despite the row, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said last year that Italy could not afford to lose the contract and the ministry statement said on Thursday the new deal would guarantee employment for around 2,000 people.
Philip Morris executives told parliament earlier this year that Italy's tax system encouraged widespread smuggling.
The finance ministry said on Thursday it was working on a further deal with Philip Morris to help combat the contraband trade as well as cooperation on the production of worked tobacco.

Philip Morris's contract with Monopoli expired at the end of last June and talks over its renewal were suspended in the wake of the tax investigation. Negotiations soon resumed, albeit at a snails' pace.

The bulk of Philip Morris cigarettes sold in Italy are made under licence by Monopoli. The U.S. firm has complained that Monopoli's production costs are four times those in its own factories in the Netherlands and Germany. $1 = 1,705 lire
